preamble: Palatalization of the alveolar trill [r] to [rʲ] before front vowels (and, phonemically, elsewhere). East Slavic and Lithuanian palatalize consonants, including the trill, before front vowels, giving a soft trill /rʲ/ that contrasts with plain /r/.

examples.note: The trill before the front vowel ě became palatalized [rʲ], which is now a separate phoneme (рад [rat] vs ряд [rʲat]).

examples.from: /r/ before front vowels and in ⟨ri⟩ spellings
examples.note: Consonants are always moderately palatalized before front vowels; before back vowels palatalization is marked with i, as in noriu.
